title: Rollout safety net — KPI playlist & quick runbook
kpi_targets: quality-signal: eval-set BLEU/ROUGE delta <= -1.0 compared to baseline
adoption-signal: feature opt-in rate >= 8% of invited cohort
readiness_checklist: Owner & oncall assigned (owner: Asha, backup: Jon)
Canary routing policy configured in console (route tag: rollout-safety-net)
Traffic shaping rules validated in staging (scripts: /ops/traffic/stripe-test)
KV/prefix cache seeded for top 10 call patterns
Alerting: error-rate, p95, model-fallback rate, and cost burn alerts set
Rollback runbook accessible and validated (dry run performed)
Billing guardrails: budget threshold & auto-throttle configured
Customer comms draft ready (support + trust templates)
Legal/regulatory checklist for private customers completed where applicable
body:
Context: quick, lightweight playbook for small-to-medium rollouts where we need automated safety nets and a compact KPI tracker. This doc is intentionally terse — use as the single-page checklist + decision ladder for on-call and product ops during the first 48 hours.

How to use:
- Start with canary-1 with a narrow cohort (50 users) for 6 hours. If all green, promote to canary-2 (500 users, 24 hours). Only after canary-2 passes do we open gradual ramp.
- Monitor both infrastructure and quality anchors simultaneously — low latency + acceptable quality are both required to proceed.

Decision ladder (quick):
- If error-rate > target OR p95 latency regresses above threshold: pause traffic and invoke immediate rollback.
- If quality-signal drops more than delta: trigger model rollback to previous pinned version and notify applied-ml.
- If cost burn exceeds 2x expected rate and traffic cannot be throttled: consider temporary feature flag to reduce sample rate.

Quick actions on an alert:
1) Triage in Slack channel #rollout-safety-net (link pinned).
2) Owner assesses: scope (model, infra, routing).
3) If infra-related: escalate to SRE (pager) and flip 'limit-burst' in console.
4) If model-quality: flip model pin to previous stable version and run quick regression eval on sample set.
5) Communicate status to stakeholders via status doc: /status/rollouts/{release-id}.md

Metrics to watch (live):
- p95 latency by route, broken down by model variant
- 1-min error-rate and error-class breakdown (timeouts vs model errors)
- Model-fallback invocation rate (important for graceful degradation)
- Quality eval snapshots on top-200 prompts (sampled every 30m)
- Cost-per-1k tokens, and projected daily burn

Notes about probes & cohorts:
- Use geographic diversity in canary-2 (US-west, EU-west) but keep small sample per region.
- Use weighted sampling to include heavy-token sessions (~10% of canary traffic) so performance under long-seq is validated.

Known dependencies / quick links:
- Pre-seed KV cache job: ops/scripts/seed-kv.sh (run from staging cluster)
- Canary routing config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/987
- Alerting playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/alerting-playbook

Post-mortem triggers (auto):
- Any unplanned rollback after >10% user exposure within 24h
- Quality regression of BLEU/ROUGE beyond threshold for three consecutive reporting windows

Owner notes (ASAP):
- Run small simulated surge test for prefix caching before canary-2 (script: ops/tests/prefetch-sim).
- Confirm quantization profile used in this rollout matches the 'latency-first' profile from infra team.
- Schedule 1-hour checkpoint 6h into canary-2 to review sample quality together with applied-ml.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we enable auto-fallback to cheaper model variant on cost spike? (ops + product decision)
- Should we add a synthetic quality signal that runs in-console every 15m for a small golden set?

Appendix — quick comms template (paste into support):
Subject: Brief service update — feature trial for select customers
Body: "Hi — we’re running a limited trial of [feature] to a small subset of customers. If you see any issues, please reply here or use the support form and include your request id. We’ll keep you updated every 4 hours during the trial."

This is a working doc. If you make a change, append the edit summary with date and initials.
runway_notes: Reserve 2x burst capacity for first 12 hours
Coordinate oncall rotation: shift 08:00–20:00 PST for first 48 hours
Notify finance owner if projected daily cost > $8k
risk_scenarios: Latency spike tied to KV cache miss — mitigations: pre-warm cache, increase shared cache size
Quality regression from model variant mismatch — mitigation: immediate pin to stable model and run evaluation
Unexpected cost burn due to high token lengths — mitigation: enable token cap for sampled traffic
